claims.nodeLabel: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA
claims.text: This was the first year Burlison's UAP disclosure amendment advanced to a House floor vote; a similar proposal failed to advance in the previous year's defence bill cycle. The measure now goes to the Senate.

a.label: Burlison UAP Records Disclosure Amendment, FY2027 NDAA

edges.label: Would extend statutory disclosure to contractors holding covered records
edges.note: The only proposed mechanism that would convert FFRDC holdings into records reachable by an independent review board with subpoena power, without sponsoring-agency consent.

a.label: Burlison UAP Records Disclosure Amendment, FY2027 NDAA

b.label: UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (S.Amdt. 797 to S. 2226; Division G of the Senate-passed FY2024 NDAA)

edges.label: Revives the review board and eminent-domain-era disclosure architecture stripped in 2023
edges.note: The FY2027 amendment restores the Senate-confirmed UAP Records Review Board with subpoena authority and a statutory transfer timeline to NARA.

b.label: Burlison UAP Records Disclosure Amendment, FY2027 NDAA

edges.label: Author of the House-adopted UAP records disclosure amendment
edges.note: Revised text designated Version 2 on 15 July 2026 and adopted as part of the FY2027 NDAA later that month.

b.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

edges.label: author
edges.note: The House adopted his Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act amendment on 23 July 2026, creating a subpoena-empowered review board and contractor disclosure obligations.

a.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

b.label: FY2024 NDAA, Public Law 118-31 - Div. A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C (secs. 1841-1843), UAP Records Collection; Div. G (IAA FY2024) secs. 7341, 7343

edges.label: Restores the enforcement architecture stripped from the FY2024 sections
edges.note: Sections 1841-1843 created a records collection without a review board, subpoena power or contractor reach; the 2026 amendment reintroduces all three.

a.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

b.label: FY2027 NDAA as reported (S. 4784, S. Rept. 119-127)

edges.label: House-adopted amendment against a Senate base text with no UAP provisions
edges.note: The House framework must survive conference against a Senate reported bill (S. 4784, S. Rept. 119-127) containing zero UAP provisions - the second consecutive cycle in which the subject is absent from the Senate base text. The 2023 precedent is that the eminent-domain and review-board provisions were stripped in conference.

a.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

b.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

edges.label: Would impose statutory transfer timelines on the NARA collection
edges.note: The amendment requires agencies to identify, organise, preserve and transmit UAP records to the National Archives on a statutory timeline and creates a Senate-confirmed Records Review Board with subpoena authority.

a.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

b.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters

edges.label: Statutory backstop for an executive release programme
edges.note: Burlison's own release frames the amendment as supporting PURSUE; structurally it cures each of PURSUE's defects - no timeline, no subpoena power, no reach to contractors, no Senate-confirmed decision-maker.
